title: Aliases, Prompting, and Interactive Convenience knowledge check

questions.prompt: Which topic is explicitly listed under “Aliases, Prompting, and Interactive Convenience”?
questions.explanation: The supplied Bash.pdf curriculum lists “Prompt configuration with PS1” under lesson 114, “Aliases, Prompting, and Interactive Convenience”. Review the topic in the lesson content to connect the term with its practical use.

questions.prompt: Which approach is the strongest default when applying “Aliases, Prompting, and Interactive Convenience”?
options: Skip version checks because all common environments provide the same Bash features.
Test the non-interactive invocation and document the environment variables/options it needs.
Assume that a working happy-path example proves correctness for every input.
Evaluate constructed user-controlled strings as shell commands to reduce parsing code.
questions.answer_key: Test the non-interactive invocation and document the environment variables/options it needs.
questions.explanation: Test the non-interactive invocation and document the environment variables/options it needs. This approach keeps assumptions visible and makes results verifiable.

questions.prompt: Which practice best prevents a common reliability or maintenance error related to “Aliases, Prompting, and Interactive Convenience”?
options: Use a small reproducible example, test an edge case, and record both the result and an important limitation.
Assume the command behaves the same across all versions and operating systems.
Skip invalid inputs because the example uses trusted sample data.
Treat one successful output as proof that the workflow is safe in production.
questions.answer_key: Use a small reproducible example, test an edge case, and record both the result and an important limitation.
questions.explanation: Use a small reproducible example, test an edge case, and record both the result and an important limitation. The appropriate checks depend on the target environment and should be reviewed before publishing a script.
